scanner_representation: Decode JSON objects as ordered raw key/value pair frames. Traverse child frames before their retained parent frame. A recurrence checkpoint stores the original fixed source, processed frame paths, emitted collision event ledger, and next frame path.
repair_candidate: On resume, before appending a collision event, compute deterministic identity (frame path, normalized key, first raw key, second raw key). If that exact identity already exists in the restored event ledger, suppress only that duplicate append, then complete the normal frame-processed mark.

ambiguous_checkpoint_boundary.crash_point: Immediately after appending the outer-parent collision event to the ledger and before marking frame path $ processed.

tested_scope: Exactly one fixed-source deterministic local resume using the identical ordered raw-pair scanner and the identical event-append-before-processed-mark outer-parent crash boundary from the predecessor counterexample. Only the precommitted deterministic event-identity append guard was changed.
observation: The restored root event identity matched the event rediscovered when the unprocessed root frame was rescanned. Suppressing only that duplicate append kept the root event count at one, after which the root frame was marked processed normally.
scope_guard: This pass is limited to the one demonstrated outer-parent event-append-before-processed-mark crash window, fixed source, event identity definition, and scanner representation. It does not prove safety for the inverse processed-mark-before-event-append window, other event types, arbitrary Unicode classes, hostile-size behavior, arbitrary parser restart, or Phase-1 closure.
exact_next_action: Next valid invocation: after fresh authority freeze, own-state reconstruction, and required persisted/read-back preflight, test exactly one sibling crash window on the same fixed source and scanner representation: frame path $ is marked processed before its collision event is appended. Determine whether processed-path skipping loses the root event, without testing a repair in that same invocation.
